methodological_rigor.justification: Case-control study with balanced sample size (n=35 per group) and appropriate power calculation (80% power, alpha 0.05). Statistical methods well-specified: Shapiro-Wilk for normality, ANOVA/ANCOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, generalized linear models with age/BMI covariates, Tukey-Kramer post hoc corrections. However, metastatic group fasting status unknown and not balanced with other groups; sample selection based on highest PSA values in mPCa introduces potential selection bias. Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case-control study identifying biomarker associations (ANGPTL3, Apo CIII, leptin elevated in mPCa) but lacking mechanistic validation or therapeutic evidence. Authors propose targeting ANGPTL3/Apo CIII using existing cardiovascular drugs, but no functional studies, in vitro validation, or clinical trial data provided. Translational potential is speculative without evidence that these lipid factors drive metastasis rather than reflect metabolic consequences of advanced disease.

reporting_quality.justification: Biomarker study with appropriate REMARK elements: case definitions, biosamples from registered biobanks, analytical methods specified (ELISA with CV values, lipid assays). However, ethics approval number provided but no statement of data availability or repository access. Inter-assay variability substantial (Apo CIII 25.54%, leptin 15.05%); intra-assay variability acceptable. Sample collection timing spans 2010-2021 but collection procedures and storage standardization not fully specified.

novelty_literature.justification: First to simultaneously quantify ANGPTL3, Apo CIII, leptin, and PCSK9 in metastatic versus localized prostate cancer, extending prior knowledge of lipid dysregulation in cancer. However, finding that triglycerides/leptin elevated in mPCa aligns with known lipid metabolism in advanced cancer. Therapeutic hypothesis (targeting ANGPTL3) not novel; suggests applying existing cardiovascular drugs to oncology without mechanistic validation specific to prostate cancer.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written manuscript with clear methods, comprehensive results tables and correlation matrices effectively visualizing relationships. Introduction appropriately contextualizes lipid dependence of cancer and gaps in knowledge. Discussion thoughtfully compares findings to prior cancer studies. Figures clearly illustrate group differences and correlations. Minor issue: methods section slightly dense but comprehensive.

key_strengths: Well-designed case-control study with appropriate sample size, power calculation, and rigorous statistical analysis including covariate adjustment for age and BMI
Simultaneously quantifies multiple lipid-metabolism proteins (ANGPTL3, Apo CIII, leptin, PCSK9) in metastatic PCa for first time
Clear demonstration that lipid dysregulation is specific to metastatic phase (triglycerides 2.3 vs 1.7 mmol/L in mPCa vs controls, p=0.0004; Apo CIII 159.9 vs 110.7 µg/mL, p=0.0179)
Thoughtful correlation analyses validate known lipid associations and identify novel relationships specific to cancer groups
key_concerns: Metastatic PCa group fasting status unknown versus other groups (fasted); potential confounding due to metabolic state differences
Biomarker associations demonstrated but lack mechanistic validation; no functional studies showing ANGPTL3/Apo CIII causally drive metastatic progression
Therapeutic hypothesis based on correlation without in vitro or animal model evidence; feasibility of repurposing cardiovascular drugs unaddressed
Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; cannot determine if lipid dysregulation drives metastasis or reflects metabolic consequences
mPCa sample selection based on highest PSA values may introduce selection bias toward more aggressive phenotypes
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sound biomarker case-control study identifying associations in metastatic prostate cancer but lacking mechanistic or therapeutic validation. Appropriate for Tier 4 journals publishing discovery biomarker studies; minor revisions needed to clarify fasting status confounder.
